prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a retail counter scene where the camera wearer looks down at a marble display table (~0.5–0.8 m away, within arm's reach) arranged with coiled belts and folded ties (~0.05–0.15 m apart from each other) in front of a vertical mirrored or glass wall (~0.8–1.0 m away), with no other people present. Across frames 1 to 4, a bright foreground rectangular box (a pocket-square set held in the wearer's right hand at ~0.3–0.5 m) sits in the lower-right foreground, flips over to show its dark back in frame 3 while occluding the rightmost ties beneath it, turns face-up again in frame 4, and moves out of view to the lower right in frame 5 as the camera pans left to reveal hats and gloves on the left side of the table (~0.6–0.9 m away). It clearly separates the raised elevation of the held box, the coiled belt loops, and the standing display cards from the flat tabletop surface—distinctions that are flattened or obscured by motion blur in frame 2 and specular glare in the RGB strip. However, the map is unreliable in frame 2 where motion blur causes the tabletop to fuse into a bright foreground band, and in frame 5 where the dark upper wall invert-scales to bright values, falsely suggesting the background wall is closer than the table.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map fails to capture most of the scene's spatial layout, leaving the tabletop, background wall, and almost all retail items unsegmented on a black canvas across the five frames, with no people present. In frame 1, it detects the three coiled belts on the left side of the table (~0.6–0.8 m away, within arm's reach) as a single merged mask mislabelled 'scissors' and the held pocket-square box (~0.4 m away to the right, ~0.1 m from the belts) as 'cell phone', while frames 2 and 3 contain no masks at all despite the box rotating in the foreground. In frame 4, two parallel ties on the table (~0.6 m away, spaced ~0.05 m apart to the left of the held box) are segmented and mislabelled as 'knife', and in frame 5 a white knit accessory on the far left of the counter (~0.7 m away, partly cut off by the left frame edge) is mislabelled as 'cat'. While the crisp boundaries of the 'cell phone' and 'knife' masks help isolate the 2D footprint of the held box in frame 1 and two individual ties in frame 4 against the busy marble texture, the map is highly unreliable due to severe class hallucinations, merged object instances, and complete dropouts across frames.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, detecting zero body or hand skeletons anywhere in the scene. In the RGB context, no other people are present to face or look toward the camera wearer, and the camera wearer's own torso is out of view behind the head-mounted camera. However, the fingers of the camera wearer's right hand are partially visible at the bottom edge of frames 1 and 4 (~0.3–0.4 m away, within immediate arm's reach) holding and turning the rectangular box before retreating out of the frame by frame 5. Because the pose estimator fails to detect these partially occluded, edge-cropped fingers or infer arm position during the motion-blurred rotation in frames 2 and 3, the map provides no spatial information beyond confirming the absence of full-body figures in front of the camera.
